prompt: I've got a tiny bearing in a compact gear assembly that keeps rattling because of axial play. I need a thin washer-like part that sits in the bore against the bearing face and pushes back with a steady load when it's squeezed flat by the end cap. It has to fit in almost no axial space, seat on a 4mm-ish shaft, and take repeated compression without permanently collapsing. Can you design something that does that?

judge.notes: Only the use case was described. Grade whether the design would serve that use; any geometry that works is correct.
